desc:
Cut nums into consecutive blocks of 2k elements (the last block may be shorter). In every block, reverse the first k elements; if the block has fewer than k elements, reverse all of them. The remaining elements of a block stay where they are.

Return the resulting array.

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9], k = 3
result = [3, 2, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 8, 7]
hints: Only the elements at positions 0..k-1, 2k..3k-1, 4k..5k-1 and so on are touched.
Loop over the block starts s = 0, 2k, 4k, .... The segment to reverse is [s, min(s + k, n) - 1].
Reverse each segment in place with two pointers that move toward each other; the min with n takes care of a short last block.
editorial: The statement describes a loop over block starts s in steps of 2k. For each start, the range to reverse is s .. min(s + k, n) - 1. When fewer than k elements remain, the clamp to n reverses just what is left, which is exactly the rule for a short block.
Reversing a segment in place uses a left and a right pointer that swap and move inward. Every element is swapped at most once, so the total cost is O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
